MB5-N6-01: withdrawn by its author after the screen return: Rank 3 cannot be met once the largest absolute value is readable at a glance. Every option must then be (top number) + (another listed number), or it is struck as the screener did. If the top number is positive, the key adds the most negative number, so the key is the SMALLEST such sum (rank 1). If it is negative, the key adds the largest positive, so it is the LARGEST (rank 4). Making the top two hard to tell apart (8.45 vs 8.5) would only move the tell into the decimal comparison and break FORM on the sums. Withdrawn rather than forced.
MB5-N6-02: withdrawn by its author after the screen return: The options are the +/-a +/- b set under a stem that fixes the signs. Quadrant IV's opposite signs strike both +/-(a+b) whatever the numbers, and the only real errors are those four values. The coordinator's note confirms changing numbers cannot fix this. Withdrawn.
MB5-N7-01: withdrawn by its author after the screen return: Sign strike cannot be removed. Removing it needs all four options to share the key's sign, and LONE refuses a single option of the other sign. An exhaustive search over 75 decimal/fraction/mixed factors, 1-4 negatives and keys 3-99 found NO same-sign set. The errors searched were: one factor omitted, divided by a factor, mixed-number sign split, pair products added, and wrong sign. FORM (an integer key needs integer options in its parity or last-digit class), HUB and rank 1 kill every candidate. Only 2-and-2 sets survive ({-8,-6,6,8}, {-24,-14,24,54}), and in every one of them the negative count strikes both positives.
MB5-N7-03: withdrawn by its author after the screen return: Kills cannot be removed at rank 3. If every option is positive, the key needs two smaller positive integer errors. The only real one is the partial answer |quotient|. The addition error A - |Q| falls below A/|Q| only when |Q| < 2, which makes |Q| non-integer and breaks FORM. Shifting the decimal in the quotient gives x10 (HUB) or a non-integer (FORM). If every option is negative, no real error lands between the key and 0. So rank 3 needs the sign error -n and a second negative, and the sign rules strike both. The |n| < 48 bound also strikes the multiply-instead-of-divide error (A x |Q|) and the sizes-added error (A + |Q|). After that, only additive errors remain on the positive side.
